item.title: Like a Bird's Nest — Wed Oct 28, 1:00 PM — Pix Film Gallery
item.description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom
FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.
This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

item.title: Women Who Build [Edition 2.0] — Wed Oct 28, 6:30 PM — MottoMotto Cafe
item.description:
Address: MottoMotto Cafe Toronto, ON Canada
Women Who Build is back for Part Two! 🍂 With GHC on pause this year, we didn’t want the season to pass without a space for Toronto’s early-career women in tech to come together. So we’re bringing the room back, cozier this time. Whether you came to our first event or this is your first time hearing about us, you’re so welcome here. Come solo, bring a friend, or bring your whole group chat. No networking pressure, no elevator pitches. Just good company and honest conversation. This time, we’re joined by Aditi Lohtia, UWaterloo Engineering alum, for a talk on taking up space as women and…
Hosted by Mairah & Jadiha

This is a meetup for AI game devs who are actively using AI tools and agentic workflows to build video games. It will be a cross between a meetup and a demo event (food and drink will be provided). item.title: Imaginary Expedition — Fri Nov 6, 6:00 PM — Burdock Music Hall
item.description:
Imaginary Expedition is a Toronto-based duo of Victoria Dobbs and Glyph Greenleaf who combine folk songwriting with early music composition techniques and intimate, unamplified performance practice. The ensemble draws people closer, quietly pushing the limits of what can be achieved with only their alto and baritone voices and a classical guitar. Their songs alternate between the lead vocalists, and gravitate toward duets with equal importance on both vocal lines.
The name Imaginary Expedition reflects the experience the duo creates. Their songs spark daydreams and send listeners on journeys through memory, grief, gratitude, and self-reflection. Their lyrics journey through emotional terrain shaped by the vivid changing seasons of the North, with imagery drawn from great lakes, old-growth forests, open prairies, wetlands, shield rock, and luminous skies.

item.title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons — Fri Nov 6, 8:00 PM — The Assembly Theatre
item.description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?
Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.
Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.
The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.
Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; Th

item.title: Refrigerator Stories: A Search for Home — Fri Nov 6, 8:00 PM — Tranzac
item.description:
(Living Room)
A new solo show by Jos Dirkx, directed by Reena Dutt, with music direction by Sacha Hoedemaker. Nine real-life stories, six original songs: starting in a classroom in Dakar with eleven kids from eleven countries, moving through Toronto, Helsinki, Juba and Athens, and arriving at a Dutch kitchen table where, at 39, Jos decides to step back on stage after all. A show about growing up between cultures, a voice that disappears and comes back, and love turning up when you least expect it. And what’s a refrigerator story? You’ll find out in the theatre.
The 2026 workshop performances will be the first time the complete show is performed for live audiences. In select venues, each performance is followed by a short conversation with the makers. The premiere will take place in 2027.
